analysis:
Reviewed three test-only changes under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD. No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or at-rest crypto paths change.

1. Fixtures/SSDCooperativePoolTestSupport.swift (head lines 1-12): the `onGCD` helper moves out of SSDCacheEpochStoreTests.swift (base lines 8-15, where it was private) into a shared test-target file. It only wraps blocking work in DispatchQueue.global and adds no security surface.

2. SSDCacheEpochStoreTests.swift: only the private helper is removed. Test bodies are unchanged, so the T-041 epoch, rotation, symlink-rejection and wipe-race coverage is retained.

3. SSDWholeRootTelemetryConcurrencyTests.swift (head lines 11-85): SnapshotDuringSweepStore takes the heartbeat snapshot on a dedicated Thread inside performExternalDestructiveChange, with the wait bounded to 5 s. This replaces the semaphore-pause design that could hold the shared SSDDiskBudget lock indefinitely. The test still exercises the real removeItemIfSafe path under evictionRoot. The assertions still check that the snapshot is available during the sweep, that the in-sweep snapshot has ttlExpired == 0, and that the final ttlExpired == 1. Only flakiness and hang risk change, and TTL sweep and telemetry-availability coverage (T-041, SEC-035 residual) is preserved.

No new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions found. Production KVCacheSSD sources were not supplied and were not reviewed. Three integration source units were omitted from replay, but the supplied patch and head text cover all changed lines.
